label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Here's the post, at about 440 words and roughly 2,400 characters.

---

A lot of you have tagged me on @Kavya's post from yesterday about founders DMing people in their own cohort's teams with 40% hikes. Yes, it is about me. Two engineers from SitterNest joined us at DabbaDost on 3 November. I would rather answer once here than reply in the comments.

First, the part I got wrong.

I knew where both of them worked from the day their applications came in. I should have called Kavya before making the offers. I messaged her only after the second offer was accepted, which is too late to count as a heads up. That is on me. Kavya, I am sorry.

This is the person who sat with me till 1am in the Koramangala office before demo day, fixing our Razorpay webhook mess when it was not her problem to fix. I have never forgotten that. She deserved a phone call from me and she did not get one.

Now the parts that are not correct. People are repeating them, so here are the facts.

1. Nobody from DabbaDost DMed anyone. We put a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and on Instahyre on 14 September, open to anyone. The first engineer applied on his own on 19 September. The second came about two weeks later as his referral.

2. The hike was 22% over their current CTC, not 40%.

3. We do have an ESOP pool. It is small, but it is real and it has been on paper since January. We did not promise anything we don't have.

I am not naming the two engineers, and I request everyone in the comments not to name them either. They applied for a job. They did not ask to be part of this.

This is going to keep happening. Foundry91 cohort 4 has 11 startups and all of us hire from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. Sooner or later somebody's engineer will apply to somebody else's opening again. So I want to suggest one simple rule for the cohort:

If you are interviewing someone from another batch company, you give that founder a heads up before the offer goes out.

I did it in the wrong order this time, so I will be the first to follow it. If the other founders in the batch agree, please say so in the comments.

Kavya, this is not a fight from my side and I don't want it to become one. You have been a good friend to me, you have helped me a lot, and I respect you. Coffee or a call, any day this week, whenever you are okay with it.

---

- **Tagging:** Delete "@Kavya" in the first line, type @ and pick her profile from the dropdown, otherwise the tag won't link.
- **Blue tick:** I left out that she didn't reply to your WhatsApp. In public it would read as a dig at her, and the post is stronger with you only owning the late message.
